regular.in_the_way: He's starting behind the curve (second rank when most people take until they're fifteen to get there), and he needs to move fast because something is trying to use his ear as a transmission line and has started forming words. The rival girl is already better than she should be. And his teacher is going deaf while lying about it, which reads like a warning.
regular.expect_next: This is progression fantasy with mechanical magic rules—singers make things happen by hitting specific notes, and there's a ranking system they climb. I'd expect him entering the school and training through advancement gates while also figuring out what that tone is and why it's trying to talk to him.

He wants the white cord — heard by people who have never met him — and he wants it before whatever is transmitting into his head finishes arriving.

mechanism.can_do: Rell hears his own pitch perfectly at all times and knows the acoustic tricks that everyone else has missed—where you stand matters more than training, and silence can be a weapon.
mechanism.in_the_way: He's competing against someone who's already ahead, his own teacher is lying about going deaf, and whatever is starting to use his head as a broadcast channel may not be friendly about it.
mechanism.expect_next: A school-based progression fantasy where the magic system has real physics underneath it. Rell is going to learn to weaponize interference patterns against rivals, and the thing in his ear is going to become a problem before it becomes an asset.

climber.can_do: She can graft abilities or traits from anyone regardless of blood relation, which is impossible for anyone else in her world. The grafts actually take on her, even from strangers or the dead.
climber.in_the_way: Every graft she takes kills an existing one she already has. She's carrying four on a system built for two, which means she's mechanically overloaded. Worse, she physically cannot refuse a cutting if it's pressed to an open cut, and people are learning this about her.
climber.expect_next: A hard-magic progression fantasy where the arithmetic is load-bearing. She's trapped at capacity and people are going to start exploiting her inability to refuse. I expect the book to watch her navigate a world that wants to use her, and I'm reading to find out what her grafts actually do and why someone without a lineage can graft anything at all. The gate is clear: she can't keep taking without losing what she loves.

stranger.expect_next: A dark fantasy about someone carrying an ability that's slowly destroying her from the inside, set in a world with a caste system (that rank of five matters), and I expect to see her hit a limit that forces a choice: let go of something, or break entirely. regular.can_do: She can accept grafts from anyone—strangers, the dead, anything—where normal people can only graft with close kin. She's compatible in a way that shouldn't be possible.
regular.in_the_way: Her root can only sustain so much, and she's already carrying four grafts on what was meant to hold two. Every new graft kills something she already loves. And now people are learning she physically can't refuse if they press a cutting to an open wound on her.
regular.expect_next: Dark fantasy built on a grafting system where power/ability is literally rooted. The book will probably track what happens when a uniquely gifted person has a uniquely exploitable weakness, and what people do when they figure out how to use it.

mechanism.in_the_way: She can't refuse a graft if someone presses it to an open cut on her skin. Every graft she accepts requires a death—something she already loves stops. People are already working out that they can use this against her.
mechanism.expect_next: A progression fantasy where the hard mechanic drives the plot forward. She'll end up in situations where she has to choose what dies, and people will weaponize her inability to say no. The book probably investigates what she sacrifices and who knows enough about her to exploit it.

climber.can_do: She knows a shortcut to heat-judgment that works the first time—something everyone else needs twenty years to learn through trial in darkness. She also dies and comes back as a nine-year-old in a world where nobody would guess that about her.
climber.in_the_way: She's two rungs up a progression ladder and can't move her father without being four. Everything she learns requires her body to change in permanent ways. The tool-making family knows she has something (the stone) and wants to know where it came from.
climber.expect_next: A progression fantasy where she goes to school and uses her technical advantage to climb faster than expected, and where the stone and the family's interest in it become a friction point. Probably exploring whether she can actually reach the rung she needs and what her body will look like when she does.

stranger.can_do: She sees something about heat and metal that took everyone else twenty years in the dark to learn—she can do it in daylight because she brought knowledge from a different world.
stranger.in_the_way: She only has one trick, not a craft. Her father is locked in a state only someone much more powerful than her can unlock. And someone already wants to know where she came from, which means her advantage is already suspect.
stranger.expect_next: A progression fantasy. She goes to school to get stronger, learns what the system actually is, figures out what the stone is and why it matters, probably becomes powerful enough to help her father, and discovers what the fourth thing means and why she's here.
open_questions: What is the fourth thing and why is that her goal?

regular.can_do: She carries precision knowledge from her past life in industrial metalwork—she understands how materials behave under heat in ways that nobody here, working by feel in darkness, has ever had to know.
regular.in_the_way: She's only two rungs up and needs four to save her father. The family that makes all the tools wants her stone and knows she's different. The craft takes your body piece by piece, and twenty years of learning in darkness waits ahead.
regular.expect_next: A progression fantasy rooted in a real craft system. She'll head to Ashvane, figure out what she's becoming, try to climb the ranks before the family catches up, and find out if her edge is big enough to matter.
open_questions: What is the stone and why does the family want it?
What does it mean to become the fourth thing?
Will she actually make it to four rungs, or is that goal too far away?

mechanism.can_do: She knows heat and magnets from her old world, so she can judge steel temperature by its color alone—a trick that gives her first-try success where experienced smiths need years of trial in the dark.
mechanism.expect_next: A progression fantasy where she climbs the smithing hierarchy through technical knowledge rather than raw talent; the school at Ashvane probably forces her to compete against people who've trained in the dark their whole lives.
mechanism.in_the_way: Her father needs someone four rungs above him willing to hold him through screaming for six hours. She's two rungs. Everything she gains has a bodily cost, and someone wants to know where she got her stone.

climber.can_do: He can apply systematic biological knowledge to manipulate a magic system that most practitioners treat as intuition, and he's got a companion AI that can read his own body back to him as diagnostic feedback.
climber.in_the_way: He's lost everything and everyone from his old world except the AI. He's trapped in a child's body learning a magic system from first principles while other practitioners treat it as second nature. The biology degree only works as an advantage if the world's magic actually respects that translation.
climber.expect_next: A slow-burn progression story where the appeal is watching him systematically unlock magic through biology instead of talent or innate sensitivity. Academy arc incoming, probably with some friction between his methodical approach and how wizards normally learn. The larger plot lives somewhere downstream of that.

stranger.in_the_way: He wakes up as a child in a place he doesn't understand. He's the only survivor from his world, so he's alone except for an AI that's somehow merged with him in ways that aren't explained. The magic system is complex and learning it is slow.
stranger.expect_next: School-based progression fantasy. He'll figure out how biology and magic connect, the merged AI will either become his greatest tool or his biggest problem, and it'll be character-focused rather than action-heavy. The back-cover tells me most of the first act, so the interest is in how it actually plays out, not what happens.

regular.in_the_way: He's starting over as a child with no context, no home language probably, no social standing. Everything is new except the AI voice in his head and his memory of how living things work. The AI is all he has left but also the thing that makes him alien to this world.
regular.expect_next: A progression fantasy academy story where he slowly figures out the rules of magic by treating it like cellular biology. The premise promises system-building rather than just hand-waving, which means I'm expecting to actually *learn* something alongside him, the way Mother of Learning does it.
